quotes_used_verbatim: A muster station is a designated emergency assembly point on a cruise ship where passengers must report during safety drills or real emergencies.
access everything they need right from their smartphone or the stateroom TV
visit their assembly station, where the crew can verify they've completed the process
there are no shortcuts when it comes to safety
primary_sources.attribution: Quoted as Royal Caribbean's description of its own Guest Safety Briefing / Muster 2.0 implementation, and labelled as one line's implementation in the article.

claims.regulatory_statement: The article says international maritime regulation requires a muster for embarking passengers around departure, stated in general terms WITHOUT citing a specific SOLAS regulation number, chapter or timing requirement, because no regulatory text was fetched in session. A convention name appeared in a search summary and was deliberately NOT printed as a citation.
claims.not_claimed: NO claim that all lines use the two-part app-plus-verification format (the article says most major lines and states that ships vary and some still run traditional assemblies). NO specific time limit or deadline figure. NO claim about how any line penalises non-completion beyond being chased. NO claim about where every line prints the muster station assignment - phrased as 'lines commonly' with the advice to check card and app and ask crew.
claims.editorial: The do-it-the-moment-you-board advice, the walk-the-route point, and the observation that a crowd in the sun absorbs nothing are the site's own reasoning.
claims.authority_deferral: The article states explicitly that the daily programme and cabin TV are authoritative for the reader's own sailing, not this page.

voice_audit.scope: full article body (itemprop=articleBody), not the summary
voice_audit.machine_tell_scan: 0 banned cruise-marketing terms, 0 generic AI tells, 0 copulative-avoidance constructions (serves as / stands as / represents a / embodies / marks a / constitutes), 0 translationese terms, 0 inline self-correction leakage, 0 ellipses.
voice_audit.corpus_comparison: em-dash density and sentence-length variance compared against four published InTheWake articles (cruise-tipping-2026, what-cruise-actually-costs-2026, great-stirrup-cay-changes-2026, cruise-pool-lifts-accessibility-gap), whose measured em-dash densities span 7.7-16.0 per 1000 words. This page falls inside that range.
voice_audit.corrections_applied: cruise-passport-or-birth-certificate: 'careful rather than comprehensive' changed to 'careful rather than complete' (one generic-AI-tell hit). No other page required an edit.
voice_audit.honest_limit: This attestation records a mechanical scan plus author judgment. It measures the presence of known tells and structural variance; it cannot certify that the prose reads as lived experience to a human reader.
